newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France, unions disagree on strike's impact.
newsitem.headline: Air France, unions disagree on strike's impact.

text.p: Unions representing striking pilots at state-owned Air France Europe said their walkout grounded nearly one third of the carrier's flights on Thursday while management said operations were barely affected.
The pilots, who began the walkout seven days ago, are protesting against wage cuts and working conditions under a planned merger between Air France Europe and its international parent Air France.

The unions said 31 percent of the airline's flights on Thursday had been cancelled while Air France Europe, formerly known as Air Inter, said it was offering "virtually full" service and that 90 percent of its scheduled flights would be in the air on Friday.
The USPNT, SPAF and SNPNAC unions said in a statement that the strike was turning in the pilots' favour.
Air France Chairman Christian Blanc is preparing a merger of the two airlines to ready the group for privatisation and boost competitiveness.
The plan would put Air France Europe crews on the same pay scale and rosters as Air France counterparts, involving a pay cut of around 15 percent.
